title: The master graph feeds derived views.
intro: The master graph holds shared facts. Projections select, reshape and combine those facts into derived graphs.
rule: Every graph space declares one master graph. Each derived graph is connected to it, directly or through other projections.
limit: Each graph has its own revision. An update can be visible in one projection before another catches up.

frames.title: Start with shared facts
frames.copy: The master contains the infrastructure facts. Two projections have consumed master revision 12.

frames.title: A fact changes
frames.copy: A network observation changes the master to r13. Derived graphs still show their previous revisions.

frames.title: Service view advances
frames.copy: The service projection consumes the master change and commits its own r9.

frames.title: Business view advances
frames.copy: The business projection now commits r5. The graph identities stayed the same throughout.

title: Events, batches, files and gRPC use async streams.
intro: An event feed, a finite file, a batch job and a gRPC client can all supply the same ordered asynchronous sequence.
rule: Preserve the input order, event boundaries and logical-time controls when changing batch sizes.
limit: Each record in a transport batch can be accepted or rejected. Each projection commits its changes independently.

frames.title: Events arrive
frames.copy: Three ordered records arrive separately.

frames.title: Batch the delivery
frames.copy: The same records travel together. Their order and boundaries remain visible.
frames.formula: Batch [A, B, C] preserves three record boundaries

frames.title: Read a finite file
frames.copy: A file reader yields the same ordered stream, then completes.

frames.title: Use gRPC
frames.copy: The delivery can stay open. The engine still observes individual ordered inputs.
frames.formula: Same initial state + rules + inputs + time → same result

title: Adapters map native records to graph observations.
intro: Each adapter interprets a versioned native format and produces entity candidates, relationship candidates, properties and evidence.
rule: The first families are Hubble/Cilium, Azure Resource Graph, Kubernetes, Azure Network Watcher and OpenTelemetry.
limit: Kubernetes Events provide observations. Removing resources absent from an ARG result requires a declared coverage and reconciliation policy.

frames.title: A Hubble flow arrives
frames.copy: A native network observation identifies an API endpoint, a database endpoint and the flow verdict.

frames.title: Produce a graph observation
frames.copy: The adapter proposes endpoint identities and an observed Calls relationship, with the native record retained as evidence.

frames.title: Adapt a Kubernetes record
frames.copy: A Kubernetes watch record goes through its own adapter to produce a pod observation.

frames.title: Withdraw a contribution
frames.copy: An explicit deletion withdraws this source contribution. Other evidence may still support the entity.
frames.formula: Other contributions can continue supporting the entity

title: Nodes and edges carry typed data.
intro: Entities represent resources, services or other domain objects. Directed relationships connect them. Both carry an ID, a type and typed properties.
rule: A relationship has entity endpoints and its own projection-specific ID. Different relationship types can connect the same pair.
limit: Removing a node may leave an unresolved endpoint. Missing and not-yet-examined are distinct read outcomes.

frames.title: Two entities
frames.copy: Each entity has a stable ID and a type in this graph’s ontology.

frames.title: Add a relationship
frames.copy: The directed relationship also has an ID. It describes an observed call.

frames.title: Attach edge data
frames.copy: A declared property records the call’s health on the relationship itself.

frames.title: Represent observed and expected calls
frames.copy: ExpectedCall can coexist with Calls. Intended structure and observed traffic answer different questions.

title: Views share timeless entity identity.
intro: A shared identity table binds a tenant-scoped, canonical key to an entity ID. The ID persists across changes to graph type and properties.
rule: Projections reuse an identity when they refer to the same entity. An aggregate, such as a deployment containing several pods, receives its own identity.
limit: Renames, aliases, merges and splits require explicit policies and evidence for identity equivalence.

frames.title: Resolve a stable key
frames.copy: The Kubernetes UID identifies the object independently of its current display name.

frames.title: Show it in two graphs
frames.copy: Both projections refer to e17, even when they attach different meanings or properties.

frames.title: A property changes
frames.copy: A new display name changes graph state; the canonical key and entity ID remain fixed.

frames.title: Assign an aggregate identity
frames.copy: A deployment aggregates multiple pods and receives its own identity.

title: An ontology defines types and properties.
intro: An ontology declares entity types, relationship types and property value kinds. Every graph pins an ontology version and digest.
rule: Activation requires validation of the portable definition. Generated C# types are planned to check property and relationship types during compilation.
limit: A property name is local to its ontology. The same spelling in another ontology can have a different meaning and type.

frames.title: Declare the contract
frames.copy: This ontology declares Service.health as text.

frames.title: Validate a compatible value
frames.copy: The supplied type matches the declared property kind.

frames.title: Reject an incompatible value
frames.copy: The boolean value fails validation against the declared text property.

frames.title: Pin a changed definition
frames.copy: An ontology change creates a new pinned definition and requires validation of dependent projections.

title: Patterns produce bindings for later operators.
intro: A graph pattern names the entities and relationships to find. Matching produces bindings that later operators can filter, group or emit.
rule: Resolve pattern types and properties against the ontology of the selected input binding.
limit: Matching produces rows of bound entities and relationships. Emit operators define changes to the output graph.

frames.title: Declare a pattern
frames.copy: Find a Pod that calls a Service.

frames.title: Find a candidate
frames.copy: The source graph contains a matching relationship from pod-7 to ledger.

frames.title: Bind the result
frames.copy: The operator produces a row containing the matched entity identities.

frames.title: Filter the bound rows
frames.copy: A filter can retain only unhealthy dependencies. A rejected row emits nothing.

title: A projection is a configuration graph.
intro: Portable operators and typed wires describe how input bindings become an output graph. The definition can include expected structure as a scaffold.
rule: Keep selection, identity and emission explicit. The compiler owns type checks and diagnostics; the runtime owns execution and commits.
limit: The typed authoring API currently covers expressions and a subset of row composition. Portable definitions require field, type and reference validation.

frames.title: Select source facts
frames.copy: Match workload facts in the source ontology.

frames.title: Choose identity
frames.copy: A declared domain and key decide which observations describe the same output entity.

frames.title: Validate the definition
frames.copy: The compiler checks references, input fields and output property ownership.

frames.title: Reject a broken wire
frames.copy: A missing operator or wrong field type returns a diagnostic before activation.

title: Stack projections through named graph inputs.
intro: A service graph can feed a capability graph. The service projection groups infrastructure details into the entities and relationships used by the capability projection.
rule: Graph inputs name their source projection and expected ontology. Ordinary dependencies form an acyclic graph rooted at the master.
limit: Reverse lens edits use a separate command path. The forward graph dependencies remain acyclic.

frames.title: Three levels of detail
frames.copy: Each graph is separately versioned.

frames.title: Master changes
frames.copy: A new dependency changes master r30 to r31.

frames.title: Services consume r31
frames.copy: The service graph commits r13 and records the input version it used.

frames.title: Capabilities consume r13
frames.copy: The capability graph commits r7 after consuming service revision r13. Each stage has committed separately.

title: Combine graph inputs with union and join.
intro: A projection can consume multiple graph inputs. Union collects compatible rows. Join relates rows using a declared predicate or correspondence.
rule: Each input keeps its own ontology pin and graph revision. Duplicate facts need an explicit conflict policy.
limit: The recorded frontier identifies the consumed versions. Branches may reflect different master revisions; aligning them requires a separate consistency policy.

frames.title: Two independent inputs
frames.copy: One input contains observed calls; another contains expected calls.

frames.title: Union the rows
frames.copy: First select each relationship’s endpoints into a common {source, target} row schema. Union collects three distinct pairs; observed and expected relationship facts remain in their upstream graphs.
frames.formula: Union requires a declared conflict policy

frames.title: Join on endpoints
frames.copy: An equality join finds the pair present in both input relations.

frames.title: Record the consumed versions
frames.copy: The result records observed r8 from master revision 13 and expected r3 from master revision 12.

title: Map between input and output ontologies.
intro: A source graph can describe infrastructure while its projection describes business capabilities. The mapping declares how source entities contribute to target entities.
rule: Match against each input ontology. Emit against the output ontology. Validate both sides, including conflicting local type and property names.
limit: Source and target types retain their definitions. Shared identity requires both representations to describe the same entity.

frames.title: Start in infrastructure
frames.copy: The source graph pins infra v1 and describes a deployment.

frames.title: Apply a named mapping
frames.copy: The projection groups infrastructure evidence under a capability identity.

frames.title: Keep source lineage
frames.copy: The capability has its own meaning and identity. The correspondence records where it came from.

frames.title: Reject accidental type reuse
frames.copy: Emission requires a type declared in the output ontology. Business v1 has no Deployment type.

title: Aggregate dependency signals with a declared rule.
intro: A health projection aggregates dependency signals into service or capability properties. Its rule defines how dependency states determine the result.
rule: Make the rule part of the projection: for example, any required dependency failing makes the service degraded.
limit: Each health projection defines its own interpretation. A causal diagnosis would require additional evidence and rules.

frames.title: All required dependencies pass
frames.copy: The service uses an all-required-dependencies rule.

frames.title: A signal changes
frames.copy: The database dependency becomes unavailable. The service still shows its previous revision.

frames.title: Apply the rollup
frames.copy: The declared rule emits a degraded service property.

frames.title: Recovery is another input
frames.copy: When the dependency recovers, the rule derives healthy again and emits a new change.

title: A graph patch records one state transition.
intro: A graph patch describes a transition between two versions. Its edits contain before and after values, and its cause points to the inputs that produced the change.
rule: An input that leaves graph state unchanged emits no graph patch. Acceptance, progress and telemetry remain separate.
limit: Batching keeps constituent patches and their revision boundaries. Squashing is a distinct operation that can discard intermediate history.

frames.title: Before the event
frames.copy: The service is healthy at graph revision 8.

frames.title: Commit one transition
frames.copy: The changed property produces a patch from r8 to r9.

frames.title: Repeat the same fact
frames.copy: A separate delivery repeats the current health value. The graph stays at r9.

frames.title: No change, no graph diff
frames.copy: Progress advances while the graph revision and retained evidence history stay unchanged.

title: Compose patches and add signed deltas.
intro: Ordered patches compose transitions with preconditions. Signed deltas add and subtract weighted graph facts. Separate C# types require an explicit conversion between them.
rule: Patch composition requires adjacent compatible versions. Delta-to-patch conversion needs a base graph and validity checks.
limit: Signed-delta arithmetic permits negative weights. Materialization validates the resulting graph. Conversion reports any loss of chronology.

frames.title: Compose ordered patches
frames.copy: Apply healthy→degraded, then degraded→failed.

frames.title: Try the opposite order
frames.copy: Q requires a degraded starting state. Applying it to healthy fails its before-value precondition.
frames.formula: P then Q ≠ Q then P

frames.title: Add signed facts
frames.copy: F denotes one exact immutable graph fact, including identity and state. Opposite coefficients for that same fact cancel.

frames.title: Materialize with validation
frames.copy: Materialization rejects a negative remaining fact multiplicity at the chosen base graph.
frames.formula: Materialization validates fact weights at the base graph

title: Read stored and virtual graphs through one interface.
intro: A graph can hold stored facts, derive facts through a virtual provider, or combine both. Callers read a specified scope at a pinned revision.
rule: Reads pin a revision, scope and work budget, and report whether the answer is complete.
limit: Infinite extents require finite query scopes. Symbolic patches for virtual-definition changes remain an open design decision.

frames.title: Choose a finite question
frames.copy: Ask for the neighborhood of e17, at depth 1, within a fixed budget.

frames.title: Read stored facts
frames.copy: A stored index supplies the known neighbors for the pinned graph revision.

frames.title: Derive virtual facts
frames.copy: A deterministic provider answers the same supported finite scope.

frames.title: Report budget exhaustion
frames.copy: A larger scope exhausts its budget. The response identifies the examined portion and reports BudgetExhausted.

title: Derive indirect dependencies to a fixed point.
intro: A fixed-point operator can derive indirect dependencies by repeatedly adding newly justified facts.
rule: The proposed initial fragment is positive recursion over a pinned finite domain. Ordinary operator cycles fail validation.
limit: Iteration and fact budgets bound the work. Convergence requires a separate argument for the admitted language fragment.

frames.title: Seed the relation
frames.copy: Direct dependencies are A→B and B→C.

frames.title: Derive a new fact
frames.copy: Transitivity adds A→C within the finite domain.

frames.title: Reach the fixed point
frames.copy: Another iteration produces no new facts. The relation has converged for this example.

frames.title: Reject unsupported recursion
frames.copy: A recursive rule that continually creates fresh identities is outside the initial finite fragment.

title: Relate source and target through correspondence.
intro: A triple graph grammar describes consistency between three graphs: the source, the target, and a correspondence relating their elements.
rule: Correspondence records which source and target elements a rule relates. Many source entities can map to one target entity.
limit: Identity equivalence requires an identity rule. Backward updates require a declared transformation with verified lens laws.

frames.title: Start with source structure
frames.copy: Two pods belong to one service group.

frames.title: Create the target
frames.copy: The target graph contains one service entity with its own identity.

frames.title: Record correspondence
frames.copy: Transformation metadata relates both source pods to the target service. These links belong to the correspondence graph.

frames.title: Inspect the relationship
frames.copy: The linked IDs remain distinct. The correspondence can also retain information omitted from the view.

title: Declared lenses translate view edits upstream.
intro: A declared bidirectional transformation translates a supported view edit into a proposed upstream change using its rule and versioned complement.
rule: GetPut preserves the source after an unchanged view is put back. PutGet returns the accepted view after a supported edit is applied.
limit: Read-only projections reject edits. Each bidirectional rule requires validation of its lens laws and conflict handling.

frames.title: A declared forward view
frames.copy: This example exposes the source label and retains the omitted source data in a complement.

frames.title: Edit the supported field
frames.copy: The caller proposes a new label against pinned source and view versions.

frames.title: Propose the upstream change
frames.copy: The backward rule uses the complement to preserve information omitted from the view.

frames.title: Reject a read-only edit
frames.copy: The read-only projection rejects the edit because it has no backward rule.

title: Change the rule, then replay retained evidence.
intro: A projection edit starts from the previous graph and replays the deduplicated union of retained inputs in their recorded order.
rule: Queue new inputs during replay. Publish the final graph difference, and preserve eligible histories for surviving elements.
limit: Each element retains its recent N graph-changing inputs. Earlier and unchanged inputs are omitted. Lens complements are stored separately.

frames.title: Retain relevant evidence
frames.copy: Each element keeps a bounded history of inputs that changed its graph state.

frames.title: Union and order
frames.copy: The replay sequence deduplicates shared input 7 and uses original ingestion order.

frames.title: Evaluate the changed rule
frames.copy: The previous graph and retained inputs produce a candidate under the new definition.

frames.title: Emit one final difference
frames.copy: Publish the change between the old graph and the completed candidate, then resume queued inputs.

title: Project graph data into document blocks.
intro: A document projection selects finite graph data and produces typed blocks. A renderer encodes those blocks as Markdown, HTML or plain text.
rule: Block and row identities are stable and separate from display order. Document patches describe structural changes before rendering.
limit: The renderer produces output text. Editing that text requires a separately designed input mapping. Document overflow either rejects the request or marks truncation.

frames.title: Select finite graph rows
frames.copy: Choose the payment service and its dependencies from a pinned graph revision.

frames.title: Project typed blocks
frames.copy: The heading and table have stable block IDs. Table rows also carry stable keys.

frames.title: Render Markdown
frames.copy: The renderer escapes values and produces the requested encoding from the typed structure.
frames.formula:
# Payments

| Service | Health |
| --- | --- |
| Payments | Healthy |
| Ledger | Healthy |

frames.title: Reorder, preserve identity
frames.copy: Sorting changes display order. The table block and row keys remain the same, so the change is a document edit.
frames.formula: row order changed · row identity preserved

title: Verify contract laws with finite examples.
intro: The design includes compilable contracts, generated schemas and a test-only mathematical reference model.
rule: The suite checks finite patch and delta laws, schema examples, selected composition rules, and C# programs that must fail to compile.
limit: General TGG correctness, production performance, arbitrary virtual graphs and unrestricted recursion remain unverified.

frames.title: Choose a law
frames.copy: Start with a graph and a valid patch P.

frames.title: Apply the patch and inverse
frames.copy: The test-only model returns to the original graph.

frames.title: Inject a wrong inverse
frames.copy: An intentionally broken inverse returns degraded. The assertion expects healthy and fails.

frames.title: Inspect the test reports
frames.copy: The downloadable reports list the executed checks and the properties that remain unverified.
